text:
sophia: Bringing up iris-14b (int4) canary on dedi-2 fleet — running into sporadic OOMs and what looks like memory fragmentation. logs show alloc failures after ~120 tokens for some requests. anyone seen this pattern?

sophia: log snippet:```text
[2026-03-19T21:04:12Z] serve error: alloc failed: requested 512M, available 128M
kv_cache.total=3.2G prefetch=true batch_tokens=8192 concurrency=12
Traceback: serve:alloc -> kv_cache:reserve -> oom
```

ajay: hm reminds me of the raptor65b case — long contexts + aggressive prefetch -> KV cache spikes. what's the request distribution (max_new_tokens / typical prompt len)?

sophia: default route settings right now: `max_new_tokens=256`, `batch_size=4`, `prefetch_kv=true`, `prefetch_windowsize=16`

kai: try lowering the default `max_new_tokens` to 64 for the canary route and reduce `prefetch_windowsize` to 4. also temporarily flip `prefetch_kv=false` to see if OOMs stop. cheap experiment.

maria: agree. also check `kv_evict_threshold` and `kv_trim_interval`. we've seen fragmentation when eviction is too lenient. suggested quick patches:```yaml
route_overrides:
  max_new_tokens: 64
  prefetch_kv: false
  prefetch_windowsize: 4
  kv_trim_interval_sec: 30
  kv_evict_after_sec: 60
```

leo: what % of requests are hitting >512 tokens? need to know tail. current SLOs?

sophia: tail ~6% > 512 tokens, p95 latency 280ms, p99 1.1s. OOM rate ~0.7% of requests over the last 6h (on canary nodes).

ajay: ok that tail explains it. if lowering max_new_tokens is acceptable for canary, also reduce `batching.max_batch_tokens` from 16384 -> 8192 to reduce token amplification from large batches.

kai: another trick: enable `kv_shrink_on_idle` (experimental) so idle KV slots can be returned quickly. config: `kv_shrink_on_idle: true` with `kv_shrink_target_pct=50`. helps fragmentation without evicting active contexts.

maria: if you want a non-invasive quick test: curl update canary route:```bash
curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/routes/iris-14b-canary -d '{"overrides": {"max_new_tokens":64, "prefetch_kv":false, "prefetch_windowsize":4}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

infra-bot: deploy: route update requested by sophia. canary=iris-14b-canary -> rolling 3/3 pods. monitoring alert: kv-cache-usage > 70% for poda-12

leo: will watch metrics. if OOMs go to zero after flip, we have a strong signal it's prefetch+tail. if not, we dig deeper into allocator fragmentation (heap hist + jemalloc stats).

sophia: applying changes now, will report back in ~15m. thanks for quick ideas :pray:

ajay: if change is promising, we should bake new defaults into model profile: set `default.max_new_tokens=128` and `prefetch_windowsize=6` until we have better quantization memory model. file an eval run to check quality regressions with lowered max_new_tokens.

maria: i'll kick off a small eval: 1k convo prompts comparing 256 vs 64/128 max_new_tokens for perplexity and end-to-end hallucination checks. will post results.

sophia: thanks — will add load traces. simple mitigation for now; long term we need allocator+kv compaction work.

kai: note for postmortem: capture jemalloc stats with `MALLOC_CONF` and a heap profile when OOM triggers. makes fragmentation root cause much faster to confirm.

sophia: noted. will attach heap profile if it happens again. back in ~15m with canary results.
